full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Nuruzzaman, J.- These two appeals are directed against the judgment and decree dated 28.6.2003 and 29.6.2003 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Pabna and disposed of by a single judgment dismissing the Other Class Suit No. 8 of 2003 and decreeing the Other Class Suit No. 9 of 2003. Since these two appeals arises out of a single judgment for same property in between the same parties. Therefore both the appeals were heard together and disposed of by this single judgment.

2. The short facts of the above mentioned Other Class Suits, in short, are that one Syed Jamshed Hussain Choudhury instituted Other Class Suit No.198 of 1996 before the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Iswardi Upazila, Pabna for declaration of title over the suit property and also observations were made in L.S. Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1996 are void, illegal and without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff. On the other hand the Managing Committee of Marami Joykalimata Thakurani Bighraha instituted Other Class Suit No. 46 of 1999 before the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Pabna impleading Syed Jamshed Hussain Choudhury and others as defendants for declaration of title over the suit property. Thereafter the learned District Judge, Pabna vide Miscellaneous Case No.14 of 1999 transferred the Other Class Suit No.198 of 1996 to the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Pabna for analogous hearing with Other Class Suit No. 46 of 1999. Eventually on transfer the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Pabna received the suit records and re-numbered the same as Other Class Suit Nos. 8 and 9 of 2003, respectively.

3. The plaint case of Other Class Suit No. 8 of 2003, in short, is that Ka Schedule land of Mouza Marami appertaining to D.S. Khatian No. 248 Plot No. 31 measuring 11.02 acres of land, Plot No. 321 measuring 42 decimals of land, Plot No. 337 measuring 18 decimals in total lands are 11.62 acres originally belonged to Joykalimata Thakurani Bighraha as lakheraj of which Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur was the Shebat of the Joykalimata Thakurani Bighraha. At the time of C.S. operation the record of right finally was published in the name of Joykalimata Thakurani Bighraha showing Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait of Joykalimata Thakurani.

Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait for the necessity of puja archana and necessary religious functions settled the property in the name of Sree Paresh Narayan Choudhury as tenant in 1943 and issued Amalnama and Dakhila. Thereafter Shebait asked Paresh Narayan Choudhury to furnish a kabuliyat in favour of him. Paresh Narayan Choudhury on 29.1.1943 as tenant executed a registered Kabuliyat being No.7064 in favour of Shebait Kumar Birendra Narayan Roy Bahadur. From the date of settlement Paresh Narayan Choudhury got possession of the property and he had been owning and possessing the property and paid the rent to the superior landlord and obtained Dakhilas.

4. One Dalimunnessa Bibi was the original owner of D.S. Khatian No.257, Plot No.336 measuring 0.60 acres of land of the said mouza. Dalimunnessa died leaving behind her only son Pachu Fakir, who sold the Kha Schedule land on 7.6.1936 by executing a registered Kabala in favour of Paresh Narayan Choudhury. Therefore, Paresh Narayan Choudhury became the absolute owner of Ka and Kha Schedule lands. Paresh Narayan Choudhury in the year 1351 B.S. settled the aforesaid property in favour of Md. Nesar Hossain by executing Pattannama bed thereby he obtained Amalnama and Dakhila from Paresh Narayan Choudhury. However, Paresh Naraayan Choudhury did not settle 03 decimals of land of Dag No.318 in favour of Md.Nesar Hossain but due to mistake the said 03 decimals of land was mentioned in the Amalnama but Md. Nesar Hossain never took possession of the said land. Haji Alef Uddin Prang and Abdul Gafur Prang were the owners and possessors of D/S Khatian No.79, Plot No.334 measuring 0.76 acres of land of mouza Marami out of which 47½ decimals of land described in Schedule 'Ga' of the plaint were sold to Nesar Hossain on 15.12.1956 through Deed No.9747 sand possession of the sold property was handed over to him and since then purchaser Nesar Hossain was in possession of the Schedule Ka, Kha and Ga lands. Nesar Hossain had been owing and possessing the aforesaid properties through his Borgader. Amongst the suit property nature of the Plot No. 319 was pond and wetland, Plot No. 327 was uncultivated land. Md Nesar Hossain while had been owning and possessing the aforesaid property for maintaining and transferring the someone Shushil Kumar was appointed as his attorney, who for the benefit of his principal transferred Ka, Kha and Ga Schedule properties on 28.8.1975 by a registered deed being No.7238 in favour of the plaintiff Shushil Kumar Roy, the attorney of Nesar Hossain although was not in possession of 03 decimals of land of Plot No.318 but wrongly included the said property in the Schedule of registered Sale Deed. The plaintiff never took possession of 03 decimals of land of Plot No. 318, although the above 03 decimals of land was mentioned in his title deed, Except said 03 decimals of land, the plaintiff was in peaceful possession of 'Ka' Kha' and Ga Schedule lands denying all the right and title of others and paid rent to the Government revenue office. There was a pond in suit Plot No. 319. After purchase, the plaintiff re-excavated the pond and reared fish there for his family and developed the suit property. The plaintiff for last 31 years without any hindrance or obstruction from any quarter had been owning and possessing the suit lands by making its arable and nurtured some fruit trees.

5. Paresh Narayan Choudhury died leaving behind 2 sons, Pronab Narayan Choudhury and Pobitra.Narayan Choudhury and widow Shushayna Debi. The heirs of Paresh Narayan Choudhury started a rent case being Rent Case No.551 of 1956 under Section 48 of the B.T. Act against the Naser Hossain for realization of arrear rents. The suit was contested by Md. Nesar Hossain which was decreed in terms of compromise. Decree Execution Case No 8 of 1957 was started and Nesar Hossain Chowdhury paid total rent of the suit property through chalan dated 26.3.1957 and 9.4.1957. The Collector of Pabna District for realization of rent started a Revenue Sale Case being No.12662 of 1958 for 'Ka' Schedule land wherein Nesar Hossain contested the case and filed an application to recognize him as a tenant. Since Nesar Hossain was in possession of the property by purchase, the Collector of Pabna District by his order dated 27.4.1962 exonerated Nesar Hossain from the responsibility of rent on considering his prayer and the suit property was released in his favour. Nesar Hossain at the time of S.A. settlement recorded his name as per his documents, however, due to conspiracy of some unscrupulous employees of the settlement department `Ka' and Kha Schedule lands were wrongly recorded as a result PRR Khatian Nos. 249(ka) and 257/2 were published in the name of landlords, Pronab Naryan Choudhury and Pobitra Narayan Choudhury. However, both the schedules land at the time of final publication of S.A. record neither recorded in the name of Nesar Hossain, Pronab Narayan Choudhury and Pobitra Narayan Choudhury, nor in the name of the Government. Therefore, there was no record of 'Ka' and 'Kha' Schedules land, Md.Nesar Hossain while learn to know about the facts of the record of Ka and Kha Schedule lands filed an application under Section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (SA&T) before the Joint Deputy Commissioner, Revenue Court, which was registered being Case No. 35/1964-65. The Joint Deputy Commissioner, Revenue, Pabna on receipt of the case records ordered to inquire into the matter and to submit a report by the then S.D.O., Pabna Sadar, Pabna by 17.6.1965. The SDO, Pabna Sadar submitted the report stating that Nesar Hossain has right and title over the Ka and Kha Schedules land. In that report it was also pointed out that Ka and Kha Schedule lands neither acquired, nor it was recorded in the Khas Khatian No.1 in the name of the Government. In that report the SDO, Pabna also recommended to settle the same in favour of Md.Nesar Hossain as tenant recognizing his documents and possession. Thereafter, the Joint Deputy Commissioner, Pabna after final hearing on 30.6.1965 under the provisions of SA&T Act recognized Nesar Hossain as tenant of Ka and Kha Schedule lands and ordered to open and prepare a Khatian in his name for realization of rent. Accordingly S.A. Khatian No. 257 was opened in the name Nesar Hossain and in the year 1363 B.S. Nesar Hossain paid rent in favour of the Government and obtained rent receipts.

6. The plaintiff on 28.8.1965 purchased the suit property from Nesar Hossain and mutated his name with the government arid office vide Mutation Case No. 245 of 1966- 67 and paid rent and taxes to the government. The holding No. 306 was in the name of the plaintiff and lastly in the year 1399 B.S. the plaintiff paid rent to the Government. After obtaining the suit property at the time of R.S. record of right as per title and possession the record of right was correctly prepared and finally published in the name of the plaintiff. The suit property of previous Plot Nos. 319, 318, 321, 337, 366 and 334 were converted into R.S. Plot Nos. 635, 334, 573, 574, 579 and 575. After publication of the final R.S record of right the plaintiff also paid rent and land development tax to the government and obtained rent receipts and Dhakhilas. The plaintiff denying the right and title of others for more than 31 years peacefully, overtly and without any disturbance from any quater had been owning and possessing the suit property. One Shamsul Alam Dewan only for illegal gain filed an application to the Government for settlement of the aforesaid land treating the suit property as Khash land and the said application was numbered being Miscellaneous Case No. 101 of 80-81. In view of the above application the A.D.C (Rev.), Pabna directed the C.O. (Rev), Iswardi for physical inquiry and after inquiry to submit a report to him. The C.O. (Rev), Iswardi inquired the matter physically and examined the documents of the Tahshil Office including the case diary and Petition Case No. 35 of 1964-65 started before the Joint Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Pabna, who ordered to transfer the property to the new Khatian No. 257 in the name of Naser Hossain who also mutated the property vide the Mutation Case No. 245 of 1966-67, from which it was evident that the plaintiff was the owner of the property. After mutation of the suit property in the name of the plaintiff, he paid rent and development taxes up to 1987. After obtaining the inquiry report from C.O. (Rev), Iswardi, Pabna the A.D.C (Rev), Pabna found the plaintiff is the owner of the suit property and by his order dated 23.6.1981 directed Shamsul Alam Dewan to take the matter to the Civil Court, if he has any grievance, and thereby rejected the application. Thereafter said Shamsul Alam Dewan again filed an application before the A.D.C (Rev) for review of the earlier order dated 23.6.1981, who after hearing the parties and obtaining legal opinion from the Government Pleader, on perusal of the C.S., S.A. and R.S record of rights by his order dated 24.12.1982 rejected the review application on contest. The Revenue Officer of the government recognized the plaintiff as tenant and vendor of the plaintiff Naser Hossain as tenant and also realised the rent from 1363 B.S to 1399 B.S vide Mutation Case No. 35 of 1964-65 L.A. The concerned authority has rejected the Miscellaneous Case No. 101 of 1980-81 and Case No. 1261 of 1948, confirming the result in favour of the plaintiff, therefore the defendant No. 1 has no right, title and possession over the suit property save and except the authority of realization of rent and development taxes from the plaintiff. The plaintiff's further case is that there is no aboriginal in the Marami Mouza of Pabna District, however, some native Christians have been living in the locality near the suit property and only to illegally grab the suit property illegally formed a committee under the leadership of one Filip Somaddar @ Khokon, who used to live in Pabna town and lodged a petition of complaint to the Secretary, Ministry of Land alleging that some local people fraudulently and illegally possessing the property of the aboriginal people. Therefore, the Secretary, Ministry of Land directed the defendant No. 3 to inquire into the matter. The Tahshilder of Dasuriya Union office after getting the direction from the defendant No. 3 started the inquiry secretly and after ex parte inquiry submitted a report to the defendant No. 3 and allegedly recommended for taking steps regarding the suit property that to make a trust for the benefit of the local people treating the suit properties of the government Khash land. On getting the inquiry report the defendant No. 3 A.D.C. (Rev), Pabna most illegally and without lawful authority started a proceeding vide L.S. Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1996 showing Government of Bangladesh as plaintiff and the present plaintiff of the instant suit as defendant and served a notice upon the plaintiff of this suit directing him to produce the papers and documents including orders of all Mutation Cases. The plaintiff after getting the notice of L.S. Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1996 on 11.12.1996 appeared before the defendant No. 3 and prayed for time to file written statement. However, defendant No. 3 fixed the next date of the case on 18.12.1996 for filling written statement. On I 8.12.1986 plaintiff further prayed for time stating the reasons that due to shortage of time he was unable to procure all the documents to file the written statement while the lawyer of the plaintiff was awaiting for moving the application, the concerned personal officer of the A.D.C (Rev) informed the plaintiffs lawyer to move the application at 4 p.m. The learned lawyer of the plaintiff when rushed to the office of the A.D.C (Rev) at 4 p.m. for moving the application the concerned Bench Assistant informed the lawyer that defendant No. 3 suddenly at about 3 p.m. came to the office and took the only record of L.S. Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1996 and rejected the application of the plaintiff and fixed for order on 12.12.1996. Thereafter on the next date the plaintiff also prayed for time but the defendant No.3 without passing any order fixed the case on 22.12.1996 for order. The plaintiff filed a written statement on 22.12.1996 and fixed the case on 26.12.96 for order. The plaintiffs lawyer although placed the case before defendant No. 3 but he did not take any note rather from the behavior posed by him in the Court the plaintiff understood that the defendant No. 3 is biased. Then the plaintiff filed an application before the Secretary, Ministry of Land stating his apprehension that he will not get fair justice from defendant No. 3 and in view of the application the Secretary, Ministry of. Land directed the Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi to inquire into the matter and submit the report and in the meantime he stayed all further proceedings of L.S Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1996. The defendant No. 3 although got the fax massage from the Ministry of land to stay the all further proceedings of L.S. Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1996 but most illegally only for getting benefit without staying the Case, on 29.12.1996 by a perfunctory report sent the case record to the Deputy Commissioner for order. The defendant No. 3 in his report made some observations which are beyond the report and also opined that Mutation Case No. 35 of 1964-65 and L.S. Miscellaneous Case No. 101 of 1980-81 and judgment and decree passed by Munsif, Court, Pabna in Suit No. 551 of 1956 is fraudulent and concocted one and farther opined that deed of the plaintiff and his vendor, power of attorney and Kabuliyat all are fraud and forged. Further opined that the order passed in L.S. Miscellaneous Case No. 101 of 1980-81 is fraud, fraudulent and concocted and the suit property is the Khash land.

7. The defendants in collusion with each other only to grab the property of the plaintiff started the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case on the basis of concocted report, although proceedings of the said Miscellaneous Case was stayed by the Secretary Ministry of Land but in spite of order of stay most illegally with the influence of the defendants started the proceeding of the Miscellaneous case. Therefore, the order passed in aforesaid Miscellaneous Case is illegal, without any lawful authority and beyond jurisdiction which is not sustainable in law. Therefore, plaintiff has legal and lawful right, title and interest over the suit property. Hence, the plaintiff filed the suit praying for the following reliefs.

ক) বাদীর বহুকালী স্বত্ব দখলীয় নিম্ন (ক) (খ) (গ) তফশীল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তি বাবদ নালীশী নিম্ন (ঘ) তফশিল এল, এস, মিস কেস ১১/৯৬ ও তাহাতে বিবাদীগণের প্রদত্ত বিভিন্ন আদেশ মন্তব্য সিদ্ধান্ত ও কার্যক্রম সম্পন্ন অন্যায়, অবৈধ, বেআইনী, বেদাড়া, নাল এন্ড ভয়েড এনি জুরিসডিকশান এবং বাদীর ও নালীশী সম্পত্তির উপর আদৌ বাধ্যকর নহে মর্মে একটি ঘোষনার ডিক্রী দিত এবং (ক)(খ) (গ) পফশীল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তিতে বাদীর উদকৃষ্ট স্বত্ব বিদ্যামান রহিয়াছে মর্মে তার স্বত্ব; (খ) (ঘ) তফশীল বর্ণিত এল, এস, মিস কেস ১১/৯৬ এর অর্ডারশিট এর বিবাদীগণের বিভিন্ন তারিখের অবজারভেশন সিদ্ধান্ত মন্তব্য আদেশ সম্পূর্ন যোগসাজসী, তঞ্চকি, ষড়যন্ত্রমূলক, নাল এন্ড ভয়েড এখতিয়ার বহির্ভূত উইদাউট এনি জুরিসডিকশান এবং বাদীর প্রতি আদৌ বাধ্যকর নহে মর্মে একটি প্রচারমূলক ডিক্রী দিতে।

8. The defendant Nos. 1-6 and 10 and added defendant Nos. 11 and 12 of the Suit No. 8 of 2003 contested the suit by filing separate Two set of written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint. The facts of the case as has been narrated by the defendants in the respective written statements are similar in nature, except few points of facts which are as follows:

"Ka" schedule land as described in the schedule of the suit along with others property was rightly recorded as Lakharaj property of Joykali Bigraha in D.S. khatian No. 248, Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur of Natore was the Shebait of Joykali Bigraha whose name was recorded as Shebait in the C.S. record of right. However, Emperor of India was the superior landlord of the suit property. The C.S. Khatian No. 247 of No. 12 Haludchar Mouza under Natore P.S. of District-Rajshahi was also recorded as 'niskar' where in total 30.69 acres of land was in 8 Plots previous Plot No. 314 of Khatian No. 248 measuring .05 acres of land was Halot for the use of general people. Plot No. 316 of the said Khatian measuring 0.53 acres of land was unused land wherein there was a temple in 03 acres of land. Plot No. 318 of the aforesaid Khatian and Mouza also 11.02 acres of land as Debuttar pond on the said Plot. 0.42 acres of land was a jungle. Plot No. 337 was also a Halot which was used for general public. In Plot No. 317 the 1.32 acres of land was a garden. Before the time of C.S record there was a temple of Joykalimata Bigrah, which are very old temple of the locality. Many worshippers perform their worship duties and thereafter they left the portrait of Bigraha in the ponds water. The worshippers of the temple used to come from others locality and use the water of pond from the time of establishment of the temple. The water of the ponds also used for performing Puja Archana of the Bigrah. Besides it aboriginals resided on the bank of the pond also use the pond's water for their personal purpose. There is a pathway adjacent to the temple which went away towards the village, which was developed by the government. The local aboriginal also cultivate the land of Plot Nos. 316, 321, 337 and 317. They also spent the usufruct of the properties for Puja of the Bigraha. The Pond's name is Marami and the aboriginal people use the same. The aboriginal use their local language although there is no words and letters in writing to write the language of the aboriginal, however, they tried to use the same only in their verbal language. The life style and culture of the aboriginal peoples recognize their cultural heritage. The government of erstwhile East Pakistan published Dacca Gazette in 1963 and 1964 recognizing them as aboriginal peoples and got facilities of Section 97 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and became the tenants under the government. Some of them came from Rajshahi area and settled there. Although some got the landed property, however, their properties were not saved from the hand of some local greedy persons. Some people also left the locality due to disterbance of the local people. Very recent master Shamol, a student of Class-V was killed by some miscreants which is the glaring instance of torture by the local peoples upon the aboriginal peoples. Now the government of Bangladesh has come to save the aboriginal people from the cruelty of the local peoples. There is a project for development of oboriginals which is under active consideration to save them. The total land of C.S. Khatian 248 belonged to Joykalimata Bigraha as the property of Niskar Debuttar property. The suit property at the time of S.A. settlement was recorded in the Kash  Khatian No. 1 in the name of the government. The plaintiff never owned and possessed the suit property. The plaintiff is a stranger and out skier people of locality. He has no right over the suit property. The plaintiff is the resident of Shibgonj P.S. under Bogra District. He was an influential high official of T&T department, who are very expert to influence and made high-handed for doing many bad occurrence and instance for his personal gain. Plaintiff's father Syed Mokkaram Hossain Chowdhury was a Munsif, Pabna in 1950. Plaintiff's father Syed Mokkaram Hossain Chowdhury was the presiding officer of the Munsif Court wherein. Rent Suit No. 551 of 1956 Hof Nesar Hossain was disposed of. There is a signature as Munsif of Syed Mokkaram Hossein Chowdhury in the judgment and decree of the above suit. There was neither legal necessity nor any power or authority of Mr. Kumar Birandra Nath Roy Bhahadur as Shebait to transfer the property of the deity. The income of the suit properties including the pond was spent only for maintaining the temple and Puja Archana. The father of the plaintiff although was not local people, but with the help of some local peoples tried to grab the suit property by making conspiracy, and accordingly he created some forged, concocted and illegal papers and documents. Kurmar Birandra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait had no power and authority to settle the suit property permanently by estingushing the right title of the Deity's in the name of Paresh Narayan Chowhury or anybody else. In fact he had never made any settlement of the land in favour of Paresh Narayan Chowdhury. The deed of Kabuliyat being No. 7064 of 1943 in the name of the plaintiffs vendor is not original but allegedly a certified copy of forged, concocted and ante dated document only. The plaintiff, therefore, willfully withheld the original deed. The Shebait never signed the Kabuliyat nor issued the Kabuliyat in favour of Paresh Narayan Chowdhury recognizing him as tenant over the suit property. The vendor of the plaintiff Nesar Hossain created the forged Kabuliyat by false personification in the name of Paresh Narayan Chowdhury. The vendor of the plaintiff created false widow and sons stating that Paresh Narayan Chowdhury died living behind those persons and filed the Rent Suit and managed to obtain false and concocted decree. Thereafter filed the decree execution case and with the help of some unscrupulous peoples managed to make a compromise solenama and thereby obtained forged and concocted Amalnama and decree in the name of Nesar Hossain regarding the property of deity and public pathway. Nesar Hossain created the fruitless and fraudulent Pattani/ Hukumnama only to legalize the alleged judgment and decree to grab the suit property. The plaintiff also obtained some forged rent receipts in pursuance to the so called judgment and decree of the Rent Suit. They allegedly compromised the execution case treating the suit property as their own property only to procured rent receipt although the property in question was `niskar' property of deity. There is no provision in the Bengal Tenancy Act to fix rent upon the aforesaid 'niskar' property. The plaintiff created the aforesaid papers and documents in the name of House Rent Case on compromise decree and procured rent-receipts only to grab the property. The S.A. and P.R.R records of right never stands in the name of the plaintiff, however, he managed to create false, fabricated and baseless S.A and P.R.R records in the name Nesar Hossain, the vendor of the plaintiff and thereafter the plaintiff was/ is never in possession of the suit property. The plaintiff, according to the statements of the plaint never rear fish in the pond and cleared the pond. Nesar Hoasain was not the resident of Marami village nor he resides with his family in the same village. Paresh Narayan Chowdhury has no rent receiving interest under the Bengal Tenancy Act, therefore, he has no right and authority to settle the tenant in the suit property. In the Kabuliyat dated 29.1.1943 there is no statement that Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bhadur settled the suit property in favour of Paresh Narayan Chowdhury for legal necessity of deity nor the plaintiff has stated the aforesaid facts in the previous case, thus the plaintiffs above mentioned statement is barred by the principle of estoppel. S.A. record of rights published and allegedly corrected by an order of Joint Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) vide Mutation Case No. 35 of 64-65 is totally false and fabricated. On query it is detected that there is no existence of Mutation Case No 35 of 1964-65, hence, if any papers submit by the plaintiff that most be forged, concocted and manufactured. The Joint Deputy Commissioner, Revenue has got no power, legally and lawful authority to open the holding in the name of the plaintiffs vendor Nesar Hossain over the Government Khas Khatian land. Therefore, through in any proceedings if obtained any order in pursuance of the proceeding those papers are illegal, void and ab initio. The plaintiff created the papers and documents only to grab the suit property and while came to take over the possession of the suit property forcefully then the local peoples and worshippers of the deity resisted the plaintiff and their men for which the plaintiff was not able to take possession of the property. The plaintiff being unable to take possession at that time disclosed the information of the proprietorship to the local peoples and threatened to take possession anyhow and in that information the defendant inquired the matter and filed an application before the concerned authority. The authority concern inquired the matter and found that the plaintiff created forged and fabricated documents and started the Misc. Case No. 11 of 1996 and after hearing the parties the defendant No. 3 with his opinion sent the case record to  the Deputy Commissioner for necessary order. The Deputy Commissioner Pabna after due consideration of all the events and circumstances of the case rightly  by an order cancelled the mutation of the plaintiff and directed to the authority to revive the previous record of rights in the name of the Government. Hence, the plaintiffs suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.

9. The Added Defendant Nos. 11 and 12 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint alleging, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable in its present form and manner, there was no cause of action to file the suit, the suit ,was bad for defect of parties, the suit was barred by law of limitation, the suit was barred under Sections 10 and 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and Sections 42, 54 and 56 of the Specific Relief Act, the suit was undervalued and the Court fees paid by the plaintiff was not sufficient. The statements made in the plant, which were not specifically and categorically admitted by the answering defendants, deemed to have been denied specifically and categorically by them. The defendants narrated the facts of the case in the written statement which are as follows:

"Ka" schedule land as described in the schedule of the suit along with others property was correctly recorded in D.S. Khatian No. 248 as Lakharaj property of Joykalimata Bigrah, Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur of Natore was the Shebait of the Joykalimata Bigrah whose name was recorded as Shebait in the C.S. record of right. However, Empire of India was the superior landlord of the suit property. The C.S. Khatian No. 247 of 12 No. Haludchar Mouja under Natore P.S. of District-Rajshahi was also recorded as 'niskar' wherein total acres of land was 30.69 in 8 Plots. 28. Admittedly the. Emperor of India was original owner who settled the Ka schedule property in favour of Moharaj Birendra Kumar Roy Bhahadur as landlord. It transpires from the materials on record that Moharaj Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur dedicated the same in favour of the deity permanently. D.S. record of right was finally published in the name of deity treating the same as Lakheraj and showing Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait. Since then Ka schedule property belonged to deity. The plaintiff by producing a Kabuliyat dated 29.11.1943 claimed that the property including Ka schedule and other land had been given Pattan in favour of Paresh Narayan Choudhury who executed the Kabuliyat. In the recital of Kabuliyat it was clearly inscribed that the property belonged to deity Sree Sree Joykalimata Thakurani and Shebait had given Pattan the same for legal necessity.

29. Now, the 1st legal issue is as to whether a Shebait can transfer any property of deity permanently or give Pattan year to year basis. The plaintiff in his plaint admitted that Ka schedule property was the property of deity Joykalimata Thakurani. He further admitted that D.S. record of right was correctly published in the name of deity showing Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait. According to him Paresh Narayan Choudhury took Pattan by executing Kabuliyat in favour of Kumark Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur by registered Kabuliyat dated 29:11.1943 which is Ext.3. On perusal of Ext.3 it transpires that it is an unilateral Kabuliyat without supporting any Patta or Dakhila issued by the Shebait as representative of the deity. From the practice and customs at that time without Patta and Dakhila unilateral Kabuliyat is not a acceptable document in the eye of law in respect of settlement of any property by the landlord in favour of Raiyat far away to accept the same from a Shebait of a deity. Moreso, it is pertinent to mention that nothing is found in the recital of the Kabuliyat that the property in question was settled by the Shebait for the legal necessity of the Deity. The plaintiff has claimed the title of the "Ka" schedule suit land in question through his vendor Nesar Hossain who purportedly got the same from Paresh Narayan Chowdhury who also got the same by executing a Kabuliyat in favour of the Shebait of Deity namely Birendra Kumar Nath Roy Bahadur. On perusal of the recital of the Kabuliyat in question, it divulged that the executent of Kabuliyat not only included the property of Deity but also included the land property wherein temple is situated. Accordingly the Poresh Narayan and Nesar Hossain the vendors of the plaintiff also transferred the same property to the plaintiff without any correction or rectification. But it is very interesting that the plaintiff although claimed the property through the aforementioned deed exhibit 16 dated 28.8.1965 and the Kabuliyat in question exhibit-3 but in the plaint and in his testimonies P.W. 1 stand corrected the recital of the Kabuliyat and deed in question stating that 03 decimals land wherein temple is situated never settled in favour of the vendor of the plaintiff. According to the provisions of the Bengal Tenancy Act landlord can settle any property to Raiyat and Raiyat can settle the property to under Raiyat, but nowhere in the Act there is a provision that Shebait of Deity can settle the Debuttar property to any Raiyat giving right of transper as per provisions of the Bengal Tenancy Act. Moreso, property in question surely belonged to Deity not Shebait, so he is not landlord although has got some responsibility only to look after the property as managerial capacity. Therefore, we are of the view that the claim of settlement in favour of Paresh Narayan Choudhury through unileteral kabuliyat and so on Paresh Narayan Choudhury to Nesar Hossain and to the plaintiff was nothing but a paper transaction without any legal sanction, recognition and basis of title. It is a settled maxim of law that without proving his title deed in accordance with law, by filing some secondary evidence none can claim any title by dint of secondary evidence which are inadmissible in law. The doccuments in question neither produced in original nor proved in accordance with law. Some other private documents were exhibited in violation of provisions of section 63, 64, 65, 66, and 67 of the Evidence Act, a party producing such documents is not relieved of the duty of proving the execution. Even those documents exhibited in trial but the court is to be satisfied as to its execution.

30. The plaintiff by producing some copies of Rent Suit Rent Execution Case and Dakhilas in the name of Nesar Hossain issued by Paresh Narayan Choudhury showing Paresh Narayan Chowdhury as Jotddar and decree-holder, which were obtained on compromise basis by Nesar Hossain and also got the property through Rent Suit all were in pursuance of Kabuliyat dated 29.11.1943, however, those papers were not proved by examining the executant scribe or attesting witnesses. Therefore the legality of those documents is not only questionable but highly doubtful. We have already opined that Kabuliyat exhibit 3 was without any legal sanction, thus, subsequent transaction cannot be treated as proper and genuine and as such, the same cannot be sustained in law. After appreciating the recital of power of attorney and deed in question executed in the favour of the plaintiff it reveals that there is no schedule of land in the power of attorney, not only that on further scrutiny it is portrait from the power of attorney wherein 5 (five) persons including the plaintiff, were the Attornies of Nesar Hossain but deed was executed in the name of plaintiff by one of the attorney, namely, Susil in the name of another Attorney, no reason has been disclosed in the deed in question which not only cast and create cloud but also depict serious doubt about the genuinty and execution of the deed exhibit 16. Moreso, it is clearly found from the materials on record that the property of Kha schedule land was purchased by Sushama, wife of Paresh but the power of attorney exhibit 28 in question was not appointed and executed by Sushama but Poresh. In view of the legal proposition as discussed above the purchase of the plaintiff from the Attorney of Naser Hossain through a power of attorney is of no avail. Therefore, we without any hesitation can conclude that the transfer of the suit land described in schedules in favour of Nesar Hossain and thereafter to the plaintiff without any legal sanction and basis of title deed. In such circumstances, we have failed to discover any materials justifying to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree but to hold that the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court in title suit No. 8 of 2003 is not tainted with legal infirmity and perversity.

<u>Moreso, the defendant Government including the period of the erstwhile East Pakistan Government have failed to produce any notification or assessment-roll in respect of the suit land which admittedly a debuttar property, hence, as per provisions of Section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950, unless Government take over the possession of the property as provided in the law none but only Deity is the owner and possessor of the Ka schedule land and as such, Shebait will act as representative of the Government.</u>

<u>33. Therefore, we are of the farm view that by executing a Kabuliyat by Shebait of deity in the name of Paresh Narayan Choudhury was never settled as permanent Raiyat Shebait cannot extinguish or alienate permanently the property of Deity in other words Debuttar property and as such, claiming the Deity's property permanently in pursuance of unilateral Kabuliyat Ext.3 cannot be considered as legal instrument.
